summary: Flagstaff Pulliam Airport (FLG) is a public airport located about 3 miles south of downtown Flagstaff, Arizona, at an elevation of 7,014 feet, making it one of the highest commercial airports in the United States. Originally opened in the late 1940s and renamed in 1959 for local aviation advocate Frank Pulliam, it offers scheduled flights to major hubs and serves as a convenient gateway to the Grand Canyon and Sedona.
faqs:
Q: What airlines serve Flagstaff Pulliam Airport?
A: American Eagle (operated by SkyWest) offers flights to Phoenix Sky Harbor and Dallas/Fort Worth.

Q: How far is the airport from downtown Flagstaff?
A: The airport is approximately 3 miles (5 km) south of downtown, about a 10-minute drive.

Q: Is there public transportation to the airport?
A: Yes, Mountain Line bus route 4 provides weekday service between the airport and downtown Flagstaff.

Q: What is the elevation of the airport?
A: The airport sits at 7,014 feet (2,138 m) above sea level, so travelers should be aware of high-altitude effects.
transport_tips: The airport is about 3 miles south of downtown Flagstaff via South Pulliam Drive; taxis, rideshares, and rental cars are available. Mountain Line bus route 4 offers weekday service between the airport and downtown. Parking is available on-site, with short-term and long-term options.
local_tip: Frequent visitors know to arrive early on summer afternoons when afternoon thunderstorms can cause delays, and to drink plenty of water to counter the 7,014-foot elevation.
